metadata.title: Stochastic Backpropagation and Approximate Inference in Deep Generative Models
metadata.authors: Danilo J. Rezende, Shakir Mohamed, Daan Wierstra

nodes.name: Deep Latent Gaussian Model (DLGM)
nodes.statement: A deep directed graphical model with $L$ layers of Gaussian latent variables defined by $\vxi_l \sim \N(\vzero, \vI)$, $\hid_L = \vG_L \vxi_L$, $\hid_l = T_l(\hid_{l+1}) + \vG_l \vxi_l$, and $\vis \sim \pi(\vis | T_0(\hid_1))$.
nodes.statement_clean: Class of deep directed generative models with Gaussian latent variables at each layer, generated by a hierarchy of nonlinear transformations of independent Gaussian noise.

nodes.name: Recognition Model
nodes.statement: An approximate posterior distribution $q(\vxi | \vV, \vtheta^r) = \prod_{n=1}^N \prod_{l=1}^L \N(\vxi_{n,l} | \vmu_l(\vis_n), \vC_l(\vis_n))$ conditioned on data, with mean and covariance parameterised by deep neural networks.
nodes.statement_clean: Data-conditioned variational distribution implemented by a neural network that acts as a stochastic encoder of the observation.

nodes.name: Free Energy Objective
nodes.statement: $\FE(\vV) = D_{KL}[q(\vxi) \| p(\vxi)] - \E_q[\log p(\vV | \vxi, \vtheta^g) p(\vtheta^g)]$, an upper bound on $-\log p(\vV)$ obtained from Jensen's inequality.
nodes.statement_clean: Variational upper bound on the negative marginal log-likelihood, decomposing as KL regulariser plus reconstruction error.

nodes.name: Stochastic Backpropagation
nodes.statement: Computational strategy for estimating gradients of the form $\nabla_\theta \E_{q_\theta}[f(\vxi)]$ by exploiting properties of the sampling distribution (Gaussian gradient identities or coordinate transformations).
nodes.statement_clean: Family of rules for backpropagating gradients through stochastic variables to permit unbiased gradient estimation under reparameterised distributions.

nodes.name: Gaussian Backpropagation (GBP)
nodes.statement: Gradient rule for Gaussian expectations combining Bonnet's and Price's theorems: $\nabla_\vtheta \E_{\N(\vmu,\vC)}[f(\vxi)] = \E_{\N(\vmu,\vC)}[\vg^\top \partial \vmu/\partial \vtheta + \tfrac{1}{2} \Tr(\vH \partial \vC/\partial \vtheta)]$.
nodes.statement_clean: Specialisation of stochastic backpropagation to Gaussian sampling distributions with full mean-and-covariance gradient flow.

nodes.name: Rank-One Plus Diagonal Covariance Parameterisation
nodes.statement: Recognition-model precision parameterised as $\vC^{-1} = \vD + \vu \vu^\top$ with $\vD = \diag(\vd)$, giving $\vC = \vD^{-1} - \eta \vD^{-1} \vu \vu^\top \vD^{-1}$ where $\eta = 1/(\vu^\top \vD^{-1} \vu + 1)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Structured low-rank covariance representation that admits trace, determinant, and matrix-vector products in $O(K)$.

nodes.name: Bonnet's Theorem
nodes.statement: $\nabla_{\mu_i} \E_{\N(\vmu,\vC)}[f(\vxi)] = \E_{\N(\vmu,\vC)}[\nabla_{\xi_i} f(\vxi)]$ for integrable, twice differentiable $f$.
nodes.statement_clean: Gradient with respect to a Gaussian mean equals the expected gradient of the integrand.

nodes.name: Price's Theorem
nodes.statement: $\nabla_{C_{ij}} \E_{\N(\vzero,\vC)}[f(\vxi)] = \tfrac{1}{2} \E_{\N(\vzero,\vC)}[\nabla^2_{\xi_i,\xi_j} f(\vxi)]$ for integrable, twice differentiable $f$.
nodes.statement_clean: Gradient with respect to the Gaussian covariance equals half the expected Hessian of the integrand.

nodes.name: Reparameterisation Gradient Identity
nodes.statement: For $\vxi = \vmu + \vR \vepsilon$ with $\vepsilon \sim \N(\vzero, \vI)$ and $\vC = \vR \vR^\top$, $\nabla_\vR \E_{\N(\vmu,\vC)}[f(\vxi)] = \E_{\N(\vzero,\vI)}[\vepsilon \vg^\top]$ where $\vg = \nabla f$ at $\vmu + \vR \vepsilon$.
nodes.statement_clean: Gradient through Gaussian samples via the location-scale reparameterisation, producing a quadratic-cost alternative to Price's theorem.

nodes.name: Proof of Bonnet's Theorem
nodes.statement: Differentiate the Gaussian density inside the expectation, use $\nabla_{\mu_i} \N = -\nabla_{\xi_i} \N$, then integrate by parts in $\xi_i$ with vanishing boundary term.

nodes.name: Proof of Price's Theorem
nodes.statement: Differentiate the Gaussian density with respect to $C_{ij}$, use $\nabla_{C_{ij}} \N = \tfrac{1}{2} \nabla^2_{\xi_i,\xi_j} \N$, then apply the product rule for integrals twice.

nodes.name: Differentiate Gaussian density w.r.t. mean
nodes.statement: $\nabla_{\mu_i} \E_{\N(\vmu,\vC)}[f(\vxi)] = \int \nabla_{\mu_i} \N(\vxi | \vmu, \vC) f(\vxi) d\vxi$.

nodes.name: Apply $\nabla_{\mu_i} \N = -\nabla_{\xi_i} \N$
nodes.statement:
Substitute the identity $
abla_{\mu_i} \N(\vxi | \vmu, \vC) = -
abla_{\xi_i} \N(\vxi | \vmu, \vC)$ to obtain $-\int 
abla_{\xi_i} \N \cdot f \, d\vxi$.

nodes.name: Integrate by parts in $\xi_i$
nodes.statement: Apply the product rule for integrals: the boundary term $[\int \N f \, d\vxi_{\neg i}]_{-\infty}^{+\infty}$ vanishes, leaving $\int \N(\vxi | \vmu, \vC) \nabla_{\xi_i} f(\vxi) d\vxi$.

nodes.name: Recognise as expectation
nodes.statement: Rewrite the resulting integral as $\E_{\N(\vmu,\vC)}[\nabla_{\xi_i} f(\vxi)]$, completing the proof.

nodes.name: Differentiate Gaussian density w.r.t. covariance entry
nodes.statement: $\nabla_{C_{ij}} \E_{\N(\vzero,\vC)}[f(\vxi)] = \int \nabla_{C_{ij}} \N(\vxi | \vzero, \vC) f(\vxi) d\vxi$.

nodes.name: Apply $\nabla_{C_{ij}} \N = \tfrac{1}{2} \nabla^2_{\xi_i,\xi_j} \N$
nodes.statement: Substitute the identity relating covariance derivative of $\N$ to its second spatial derivative.

nodes.name: Apply product rule twice
nodes.statement: Two successive applications of integration by parts move both derivatives onto $f$, producing $\tfrac{1}{2} \E_{\N(\vzero,\vC)}[\nabla^2_{\xi_i,\xi_j} f(\vxi)]$.

nodes.name: $L_1$ Bound on Marginal Error of Imputation Kernel
nodes.statement: If for some $\varepsilon > 0$ the recognition model satisfies $\int |q(\xi | \vis) p(\vis)/p(\xi) - p(\vis | \xi)| d\vis \le \varepsilon$ for all $\xi$, then $p(\vis_m | \vis_o)$ is a weak fixed point of the kernel $T^q$ with $L_1$ deviation at most $\varepsilon$.
nodes.statement_clean: When the recognition model is close to the true posterior, the imputation Markov chain has a fixed-point marginal within $\varepsilon$ of the target marginal in $L_1$.
assumptions: $\exists \varepsilon > 0$ such that $\int |q(\xi | \vis) p(\vis)/p(\xi) - p(\vis | \xi)| d\vis \le \varepsilon$ for all $\xi$

nodes.name: Proof of $L_1$ Bound on Marginal Error
nodes.statement: Expand the kernel difference, regroup using $p(\vis)/p(\xi)$ change of measure, then bound the absolute value of the integrand by $\varepsilon$ via the assumed pointwise bound.

nodes.name: Expand kernel difference
nodes.statement: Substitute the definitions of $T^q$ and $T$ and write the difference as a triple integral over $\vxi, \vis_m, \vis'_o$.

nodes.name: Change measure via $p(\vis)/p(\xi)$
nodes.statement: Multiply and divide by $p(\vis) p(\xi)$ to express the bracket as $q(\xi | \vis) p(\vis)/p(\xi) - p(\vis | \xi)$.

nodes.name: Bound by $\varepsilon$
nodes.statement: Move the absolute value inside the integrals using the triangle inequality and apply the assumed pointwise bound to obtain the final $\varepsilon$ estimate.

nodes.name: Learning in DLGMs (Stochastic Backpropagation)
nodes.statement: Stochastic-gradient algorithm that jointly optimises generative parameters $\vtheta^g$ and recognition parameters $\vtheta^r$ by alternating bottom-up sampling from $q$, top-down generation, and stochastic-backpropagation gradient updates.
input: Initial generative parameters $\vtheta^g$ and recognition parameters $\vtheta^r$
nodes.pseudocode: WHILE not converged: $\vV \gets$ getMiniBatch(); $\vxi_n \sim q(\xi_n | \vis_n)$ (bottom-up); $\hid \gets \hid(\xi)$ (top-down); updateGradients() via eqs (\ref{eq:dFEdThetaG})--(\ref{eq:dFEdThetaR}); $\vtheta^{g,r} \gets \vtheta^{g,r} + \Delta \vtheta^{g,r}$.

nodes.name: Sample mini-batch
nodes.statement: $\vV \gets$ getMiniBatch(): draw a mini-batch of observations from the data set.

nodes.name: Bottom-up recognition sampling
nodes.statement: $\vxi_n \sim q(\xi_n | \vis_n)$ for each $n$ in the mini-batch via equation \eqref{eq:Q}.

nodes.name: Top-down generative pass
nodes.statement: $\hid \gets \hid(\xi)$: propagate samples through the generative hierarchy via equation \eqref{eq:HiddenGen}.

nodes.name: Update gradients via stochastic backpropagation
nodes.statement: Compute $\nabla_{\vtheta^g} \FE$ and $\nabla_{\vtheta^r} \FE$ using equations \eqref{eq:dFEdThetaG}, \eqref{eq:dFEdMu}, \eqref{eq:dFEdR}, \eqref{eq:dFEdThetaR}.

nodes.name: RMSprop parameter update
nodes.statement: $\vtheta^{g,r} \gets \vtheta^{g,r} + \Delta \vtheta^{g,r}$ with $\Delta \vtheta^{g,r} = -\Gamma^{g,r} \nabla_{\vtheta^{g,r}} \FE(\vV)$.

nodes.name: Convergence loop
nodes.statement: Repeat steps 1--5 WHILE hasNotConverged().

nodes.name: Image Completion via Recognition Markov Chain
nodes.statement: Iterative imputation procedure that fills missing pixels by alternating recognition-model sampling and generative reconstruction; defines a Markov chain on $\vis_m$ with kernel $T^q(\vis'_m | \vis_m, \vis_o) = \iint p(\vis'_m, \vis'_o | \xi) q(\xi | \vis) d\vis'_o d\xi$.
input: Trained generative model $p(\vis | \xi)$ and recognition model $q(\xi | \vis)$
output: Samples of missing entries $\vis_m$ approximately distributed as $p(\vis_m | \vis_o)$
nodes.pseudocode: Initialise $\vis_m$ randomly; REPEAT: sample $\xi \sim q(\xi | \vis_m, \vis_o)$; sample $(\vis'_m, \vis'_o) \sim p(\cdot | \xi)$; set $\vis_m \gets \vis'_m$.

nodes.name: Initialise missing pixels
nodes.statement: Initialise the unobserved pixels $\vis_m$ with random values; observed $\vis_o$ remains fixed.

nodes.name: Sample latent from recognition model
nodes.statement: Draw $\xi \sim q(\xi | \vis)$ where $\vis = (\vis_m, \vis_o)$.

nodes.name: Reconstruct image from generative model
nodes.statement: Sample $(\vis'_m, \vis'_o) \sim p(\vis | \xi)$ and update missing entries $\vis_m \gets \vis'_m$.

nodes.name: Iterate Markov chain
nodes.statement: Repeat steps 2--3; the sequence forms a Markov chain on $\vis_m$ whose stationary distribution approximates $p(\vis_m | \vis_o)$.

nodes.name: Variational Inference in DLGMs
nodes.statement: Find parameters $(\vtheta^g, \vtheta^r)$ minimising the free energy $\FE(\vV)$, equivalently maximising a variational lower bound on $\log p(\vV)$ for the deep latent Gaussian model.
nodes.statement_clean: Joint optimisation of the generative and recognition parameters of a DLGM by minimising the variational free energy.

nodes.name: Generative Process Equations
nodes.statement: $\vxi_l \sim \N(\vzero, \vI)$; $\hid_L = \vG_L \vxi_L$; $\hid_l = T_l(\hid_{l+1}) + \vG_l \vxi_l$ for $l = 1, \ldots, L-1$; $\vis \sim \pi(\vis | T_0(\hid_1))$.

nodes.name: General GBP Rule
nodes.statement:
$
abla_\vtheta \E_{\N(\vmu,\vC)}[f(\vxi)] = \E_{\N(\vmu,\vC)}[\vg^	op \partial \vmu/\partial \vtheta + 	frac{1}{2} \Tr(\vH \partial \vC/\partial \vtheta)]$ with $\vg = 
abla f$ and $\vH = 
abla^2 f$.

nodes.name: Free-Energy Closed Form for Gaussian $q$
nodes.statement: $\FE(\vV) = -\sum_n \E_q[\log p(\vis_n | \hid(\vxi_n))] + \tfrac{1}{2\kappa} \|\vtheta^g\|^2 + \tfrac{1}{2} \sum_{n,l} [\|\vmu_{n,l}\|^2 + \Tr(\vC_{n,l}) - \log|\vC_{n,l}| - 1]$.

nodes.name: Recognition Gradients ($\vmu$, $\vR$)
Closed-Form $\vR$ Factor
nodes.statement: $\vR = \vD^{-1/2} - [(1 - \sqrt{\eta})/(\vu^\top \vD^{-1} \vu)] \vD^{-1} \vu \vu^\top \vD^{-1/2}$, satisfying $\vC = \vR \vR^\top$.

nodes.name: Two-Layer DLGM Activation
nodes.statement: For a two-layer model: $\hid_1(\vxi_{1,2}) = \vW_1 f(\vG_2 \vxi_2) + \vG_1 \vxi_1 + \vb_1$; recognition uses $q(\vxi_l | \vis) = \N(\vxi_l | \vmu, (\diag(\vd) + \vu \vu^\top)^{-1})$ with neural-net parameterised $\vmu, \vd, \vu$.

nodes.name: MNIST Generative Modelling
nodes.statement: Three-layer DLGM (two deterministic 200-unit layers, one stochastic 200-latent layer) trained on binarised MNIST; achieves $-\log p(\vv) = 86.60$ with rank-one covariance, competitive with DBN and NADE.

nodes.name: NORB / CIFAR / Frey Faces Generation
nodes.statement: DLGMs trained on NORB ($96 \times 96$, 1 deterministic 400-unit layer + 100 stochastic latents), CIFAR-10 $8 \times 8$ patches, and Frey faces; produce visually realistic samples.

nodes.name: Missing-Data Imputation on SVHN/MNIST/Frey
nodes.statement: DLGM imputes missing pixels (60--80\% MAR and patch-shaped NMAR) on SVHN, MNIST, and Frey faces using the recognition Markov-chain procedure of Appendix F.

nodes.name: Univariate Variance Comparison
nodes.statement:
For $\xi \sim \N(\mu, \sigma^2)$ and $f(\xi) = c\xi^2/2$: $\Var[
abla_\xi f] = c^2 \sigma^2$, $\Var[
abla_{\xi^2} f] = 0$, $\Var[(\xi - \mu)/\sigma \cdot 
abla_\xi f] = 2c^2\sigma^2 + \mu^2 c^2$, $\Var[	extrm{REINFORCE}] = 2c^2\mu^2 + (5/2) c^2 \sigma^2$, demonstrating GBP variance dominates REINFORCE.

nodes.name: REINFORCE Variance Scales as $O(K)$ vs GBP $O(1)$
nodes.statement: For separable $f(\xi) = \sum_i f(\xi_i)$ with bounded per-term variance, $\Var[\textrm{GBP}] = O(1)$ while $\Var[\textrm{REINFORCE}] = O(K)$, motivating the use of stochastic backpropagation.

nodes.name: DLGMs Generalise Factor Analysis and NLGBN
nodes.statement: One-layer DLGM with linear $T$ recovers factor analysis; with $T_l(\hid) = \vA_l f(\hid) + \vb_l$ recovers non-linear Gaussian belief networks (Frey 1999).

nodes.name: Algorithmic Complexity $O(L \bar{K}^2)$
nodes.statement: Sample generation and per-training-sample cost are both $O(L \bar{K}^2)$, matching that of an auto-encoder of comparable depth.

nodes.name: REINFORCE
nodes.statement: Likelihood-ratio gradient estimator $\nabla_\theta \E_p[f(\xi)] = \E_p[(f(\xi) - b) \nabla_\theta \log p(\xi | \theta)]$ with baseline $b$ for variance reduction.

nodes.name: Wake-Sleep Algorithm
nodes.statement: Two-phase training procedure for layered belief networks alternating bottom-up recognition and top-down generation updates without optimising a single consistent objective.

nodes.name: RMSprop
nodes.statement: Per-parameter adaptive learning-rate heuristic that divides the gradient by a running average of its recent magnitude.

nodes.name: Fundamental Theorem for Markov Chains
nodes.statement: An aperiodic, irreducible Markov chain with a stationary distribution $\pi$ generates samples that converge in distribution to $\pi$.
